notes.2: Makes 2 loaves. Bake them on two sheet pans, one rack in the upper third and one in the lower third, and swap them halfway.

move.title: A rich dough, braided
move.body: Challah is a yeast dough made rich with eggs, honey, and oil. It rises, is rolled into three ropes and braided, rises again, and bakes golden under an egg wash until it reads 190°F inside.

callback.body: Pita is a lean dough: flour, water, yeast, a little oil. Challah adds eggs, honey, and more oil. They make the bread soft and golden, but they also slow the yeast down, so this dough takes longer to rise.

why.title: Why a rich dough rises slowly
why.body: Fat coats the gluten strands, and sugar pulls water away from the yeast. Both slow it down. That's why challah's first rise is about an hour and a half, where pita's is one hour.

why.title: The windowpane test
why.body: Stretch a small piece of dough between your fingers. If it goes thin enough to let light through without tearing, the gluten is strong enough to hold the rise and the braid. If it tears, knead 2 more minutes and test again.

why.title: Even ropes
why.body: Ropes of the same weight and length make a braid that bakes evenly. A thick rope stays doughy while a thin one overbakes.

why.title: Egg wash
why.body: The proteins and sugars in egg brown deeply and shine in the oven. A wash brushed on before the second rise and again before baking gives an even, glossy crust.

why.title: Why a foil tent
why.body: Honey and egg brown fast. If the top is deep brown before the middle is done, a loose sheet of foil shades it while the inside finishes baking.

why.title: 190°F inside
why.body: A rich bread is done when its center reaches 190°F. By then the starch has set, so the crumb is soft but not gummy. Color alone can fool you, because the crust browns early.

wrong.sign: The braid came apart or spread flat
wrong.fix: Braid a little tighter next time, and pinch and tuck both ends well under the loaf.

wrong.sign: The top is brown, but the middle reads under 190°F
wrong.fix: Lay foil loosely over the top and bake 5 more minutes, then check again.

wrong.sign: The loaf split along one side
wrong.fix: It went in the oven before its second rise was done. Next time, wait until it's puffy and a gentle poke springs back slowly.
It came out under 190°F, or it was sliced hot. Check the temperature, and let it cool at least 30 minutes.

quiz.q: Why does challah rise more slowly than pita?
choices: Its eggs, honey, and oil slow the yeast down
quiz.explain: Fat coats the gluten and sugar pulls water from the yeast.

quiz.q: What temperature tells you a challah is done?
quiz.explain: The crust browns early, so the thermometer is the sure test.

quiz.q: What does the windowpane test check?
choices: That the gluten is strong enough
That the dough is warm enough
quiz.explain: Dough that stretches thin without tearing can hold the rise and the braid.

ingredients.text: a little more, for the bowl

steps.text: Warm the water in the measuring cup in the microwave for about 20 seconds. Stir and check it with the thermometer. It should read 105 to 110°F.
steps.tip: Too hot? Let it sit a minute and check again.

steps.text: Pour the water into the large bowl. Stir in 1 teaspoon of the honey, then sprinkle the yeast over the top. Leave it alone to bloom.
steps.look: A layer of foam on top, and it smells like bread.

steps.text: Add the rest of the honey, the ¼ cup of oil, the salt, and the {n:egg} eggs for the dough. Whisk them in with the fork.
Wash your hands with soap, and throw away the eggshells.
steps.tip: Raw egg can carry Salmonella. Wash before you touch anything else.

steps.text: Add the flour and stir with the wooden spoon until a soft, shaggy dough forms.
steps.tip: Don't taste the raw dough. It has raw egg and raw flour.

steps.text: Dust the counter with flour and turn the dough out. Knead it until it's smooth and stretchy, then do the windowpane test.
steps.look: A small piece stretches thin enough to see light through without tearing.

steps.text: Rub a little oil around the bowl, put the dough in, and turn it once to coat it. Cover with a towel and leave it somewhere warm until it doubles.
steps.look: Doubled. A floured finger pressed in leaves a dent that stays.

steps.text: Line the sheet pan with parchment. Weigh the dough, then cut it into 3 pieces of the same weight. Roll each into a rope about 16 inches long, thicker in the middle than at the ends.
steps.tip: If a rope keeps shrinking back, leave it for 5 minutes and come back to it.

steps.text: Lay the ropes side by side and pinch them together at the top. Braid them, outside rope over the middle each time, left then right, snug but not stretched. Pinch the bottom ends together and tuck both ends under the loaf. Lift it onto the pan.
steps.tip: This is the braid from this week's drill. If you braided from the middle out there, you can do that here instead.

steps.text: Beat the egg for the wash with the tablespoon of water in the small bowl. Brush a thin coat over the whole braid.
Wash your hands and the brush with soap. Cover the egg wash and put it in the fridge for later.
Cover the loaf loosely with the towel and let it proof. Heat the oven to 350°F while it does.
steps.look: Puffy, about half again as big. A gentle poke springs back slowly and leaves a small dent.

steps.text: Brush the loaf with a second coat of egg wash, into the cracks of the braid, and sprinkle on the sesame seeds if you're using them.
Wash your hands and the brush, and throw away the rest of the egg wash.
Bake the challah. Check it at 20 minutes, and if the top is already deep brown, lay a sheet of foil loosely over it.

With oven mitts, pull the pan out partway. Push the thermometer into the thickest part of the loaf from the side, so the tip is in the center. It's done at 190°F. If it's lower, bake 5 more minutes and check again.
Turn off the oven. Slide the challah onto the cooling rack and let it cool before slicing or tearing.
steps.tip: Slicing it hot makes the inside gummy. It keeps cooking as it cools.

move.title: Mastery: a braid you can measure
move.body: This is the unit's mastery week, so you bake it on your own: an enriched dough kneaded to a windowpane, three ropes weighed to match, a tight braid, and a loaf you check three ways before it comes out: its color, the sound of its bottom, and 190°F in the center.

add.title: Ropes that match
add.body: Three ropes within a tenth of an ounce of each other braid into a loaf that's even from end to end. Rolled to the same length and tapered the same way, the braid sits straight instead of curving toward the heavy side.

add.title: The hollow sound
add.body: Tap the bottom of a baked loaf. A set, dry crumb sounds hollow, like a drum; a wet one thuds. It's a second check, after the thermometer, because a rich loaf can sound hollow a little early.

choices: So the braid bakes evenly and sits straight
quiz.explain: A heavy rope stays doughy while a light one overbakes.

quiz.q: A gentle poke springs back slowly and leaves a small dent. The braid is…
quiz.explain: A fast spring-back is under; no spring-back at all is over.

quiz.q: The top is deep brown but the center reads 180°F. What do you do?
choices: Tent it with foil and bake 5 more minutes
quiz.explain: Honey and egg brown the crust before the center is done.

quiz.q: What does a hollow sound from the bottom tell you?
choices: The crumb has set and dried

warm-water.text: Warm the water in the measuring cup in the microwave for about 20 seconds. Stir and check it with the thermometer: 105 to 110°F.

knead.text: Dust the counter lightly with flour and turn the dough out. Knead until it's smooth and stretchy, then do the windowpane test. If it tears, knead 2 more minutes and test again.
knead.look: A small piece stretches thin enough to see light through without tearing.

ropes.text: Line the sheet pan with parchment. Weigh the dough and divide the weight by 3. Cut 3 pieces, weighing each, and pinch dough from heavy pieces onto light ones until they're within a tenth of an ounce. Roll each into a rope 16 inches long, thicker in the middle and tapered at the ends.
ropes.look: Three ropes the same length, each tapered the same way.

braid.text: Pinch the ropes together at the top. Braid them, outside rope over the middle, left then right, snug but not stretched. Pinch the bottom ends together, tuck both ends under, and lift the loaf onto the pan.

check.text: With oven mitts, pull the pan out partway. Push the thermometer into the thickest part from the side, so the tip is in the center: 190°F. Then tip the loaf up with a mitt and tap the bottom: it should sound hollow. If either check fails, bake 5 more minutes and check again.
